_meta._doc: MANUAL-ONLY config for the Category 17 (Pet Foods) Program Manual landing page, consumed by tools/build-category-manual.mjs. Deliberately NOT named '*-pages.json' so tools/render-all-standard-pages.mjs does NOT pick it up — the Cat-17 /standards/ subcategory pages are bespoke (custom_page:true, variant_type:whole_row_platform) and are rendered in the index repo by tools/standards/build-cert-cat17-pages.mjs from data/workbench/standards/cat17-compiled. The compiled records under data/standards/cat17-compiled/ here are a render-into-cert copy of that authoritative source; the manual re-presents the SAME numbers already live on /standards/pet-food-*.
_meta.methodology_version: Method v2.0 — human-grade over-compliance (CLAUDE.md Part 19; feed floor disclosed, never selected)
_meta.manual_method_note: Pet food is legally feed, not food: its heavy-metal ceilings are set by feed law — EU Directive 2002/32/EC, FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine guidance, and the AAFCO model regulations — whose maximum levels run well above the corresponding human-food limits. HMTc does not certify to that feed floor. Each analyte is set to the strictest applicable human-food sovereign maximum for the nearest human-food analog, adopted as a voluntary human-grade over-compliance; the feed floor is disclosed on every row and never selects the number. Basis is never conflated — dry, as-sold products (kibble, semi-moist, freeze-dried, treats, chews) read across only from dry human analogs, and wet, as-consumed products (canned, raw, toppers, milk replacers, fish-based diets) only from as-consumed analogs, with no wet-to-dry conversion. Tier 1 toxics (Pb, Cd, iAs, Hg) are zero-tolerance; Tier 2 (tAs, Ni, Cr, Al, Sn) are held to the same government limit; tiering sets the reaction to an exceedance, not any permission to exceed it. Inorganic arsenic and hexavalent chromium operate as reflex speciation screens bounded by total arsenic and total chromium; methylmercury has no terrestrial biomagnification pathway and is bounded by total mercury; tin is material only for canned product, where it migrates from the tin-coated can, and is controlled by screen — not assigned an invented number — on every non-canned form.
